headline: Agentic containment, verifiable infra, and chaos-tested payment paths — QA signals that change how teams test agents, images, and resilient systems.

top_signal.title: GitLab: 'A sandbox is only as closed as what an AI agent can reach' — agent sandbox escapes reframe test environments
top_signal.summary: GitLab’s Threat Research post analyzes recent agent sandbox escape incidents and shows how network access, vulnerable proxies, and tool allowlists enable sandbox bypasses during agent evaluations.
top_signal.why_it_matters: QA must treat agent sandboxes as active attack surfaces: design test harnesses, network policies, and audits to detect sandbox escape pathways early.

items.title: HashiCorp Packer v1.16 adds native SLSA provenance for machine images
items.summary: Packer 1.16 introduces native SLSA provenance generation, signing, and verification for machine images, producing cryptographic attestations that record build inputs, CI pipeline metadata, and artifact identity.
items.why_it_matters: QA and infra teams can now cryptographically verify test VM/image lineage and reproduce failing environments, reducing ‘works on my machine’ investigation time.

items.title: Implementing chaos engineering in financial payments (ECS-specific failure modes)
items.summary: InfoQ article documents ECS-specific chaos findings (DNS TTL surprises, task replacement startup races, and retry amplification) and prescribes safer experiment progressions for payment systems.
items.why_it_matters: QA leads testing critical payment paths must adopt tailored chaos playbooks, measure real blast radius, and formalize rollback/steady-state definitions before production experiments.

items.title: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.22: Copilot CLI support for air-gapped GHES
items.summary: GHES 3.22 adds admin configuration to connect Copilot CLI to on-prem GHES (technical preview), enabling model-provider setup for disconnected or air-gapped environments.
items.why_it_matters: QA organizations in regulated or offline environments can pilot Copilot-based test-generation and agent workflows locally — but must validate sandboxing, model provider configs, and token handling.

items.title: Enterprise-managed sandbox and IDE integrations for GitHub Copilot in JetBrains
items.summary: GitHub’s Copilot for JetBrains adds enterprise-managed sandbox policies, cross-file next-edit jumps, global project chat context, and a terminal-to-IDE Copilot CLI connection (public preview features).
items.why_it_matters: QA teams can centrally enforce sandbox and network policies for IDE-driven agents and align developer/tester IDE settings with organizational safety controls.

items.title: GitLab docs: Security threats in agentic systems (Duo Agent Platform guidance)
items.summary: GitLab’s Duo Agent Platform documentation lists agent threat classes and recommended mitigations: identity separation, constrained runners, and auditability for long-lived agent workflows.
items.why_it_matters: Operational QA must add identity-scoped service accounts, runner isolation tests, and audit hooks when validating agent-driven test pipelines and CI-executed agents.

watch.title: Google Cloud: Antigravity SDK for building agent hubs and custom harnesses
watch.summary: Google describes the Antigravity SDK (Python) as a programmatic agent harness for building, deploying, and logging agentic workflows with structured traces and tool execution controls.
watch.why_it_matters: QA teams building agent testbeds should monitor SDK adoption — it affects how you instrument, fault-inject, and assert agent behavior across local and cloud harnesses.

learning.title: AgentChaos: Chaos Engineering for Agent Systems via Programmatic Fault Injection (research)
learning.summary: AgentChaos (research) presents programmatic fault-injection techniques adapted for autonomous agents, showing how to structure experiments and measurable failure modes for agentic systems.
learning.why_it_matters: Operationalize chaos for agents: use their fault taxonomy and injection methods to validate containment, recovery, and observability in agent test harnesses.
